latin.589: §. XIX. Waldenses in Anglia, sub Wiclephitarum nomine, Seculo XIV. celebres, excipiunt SECULO XV. WALDENSES BOHEMI, HUSSITÆ cognominati à Johanne Husso, Wiclephi Discipulo, perque Scripta Wiclephi, ab Hieronymo Pragensi, ex Anglia in Bohemiam, delata, veram sententiam adversus Papatum egregiè edocto.
latin.590: Huic etsi idem evenit, quod, post centum annos, Luthero, (de quo propheticô quôdam spiritu prædixerat, ex cineribus anseris, i. e. suis, seu Hussi (isto nomine Bohemi anserem designant) olorem, seu Lutherum resurrecturum, (quem in cineres Papistæ haut redacturi essent) ut scilicet omnem Papatum, cui innutritus erat, simul & semel abjicere minus valeret, imò potiùs, uti Lutherus, initio Reformationis, in Indulgentiis solummodò abrogandis, sic hic in Communione sub Utraque introducenda ac statuminanda, omnem operam suam collocaret, Transsubstantiatione non minus atque Lutherus, missum factâ, quin cum Consubstantiatione eodem locô habitâ, uti patet ex ipsius Hussi Tractatu de Sacramento corporis & sanguinis Domini, quem scripsit in carcere Constantiensi Anno 1415. cap. 2.
latin.591: tamen Sectatores Hussi à regione, in qua degebant, Bohemi Fratres, ab oppido quodam, seu Castello, nomine Tabor, Taboritæ nuncupati, veritati de S. Cœna propiores accessere, agnitâ tùm tropicâ in verbis Institutionis locutione, tùm præsentia corporis Christi in Cena, sed Spirituali duntaxat, non Naturali corporalique; manducatione item ore fidei peragendâ, hincque fidelibus peculiari, nec infidelibus communi. Hæc manifesta evadunt omnia ex Confessionibus eorum variis, Seculis XIV. & XV. in publicum editis & à Balthasare Lydro Pastore Dordraceno Anno 1616. unô Volumine, duabus constante partibus, compræhensis.
latin.592: Parte Primâ Johannes Lucawitz, Taboritarum præcipuus doctor, contra Rokenzanam & Papistas Pragenses, ita de Sacramento Corporis & Sanguinis Christi confitetur: De hoc, ait, Sacramento, istud ex fide scripturæ tenemus & corde sinceriter credimus, quod panis quem Christus in sua Cœna accipiens, suis ad manducandum dedit discipulis, & in ejus digna perceptione per Ministerium fidelium sacerdotum reliquit memoriam suæ passionis, est in natura sua verus panis, qui pronomine, Hoc, demonstratur in hac propositione sacramentali: Hoc est corpus meum, & cum hoc verum corpus Christi de Virgine sumtum & pro nobis traditum, non identicè, non de identitate materiali intelligendo, sed sacramentaliter, realiter & verè, qui propter sui habitudinem ad corpus Christi, in sibi debita habendus est reverentia, & fideles illam venerantur non ut est panis substantia, sed de quanto, ut præmittitur, est corpus Christi, cujus verum corpus in eodem esse veraciter, sacramentaliter, SPIRITUALITER, est credendum. Non autem cum omnibus proprietatibus tam essentialibus quam accidentalibus consequentibus ipsum.
latin.593: Quæ verba etiam articulum primum Confessionis Taboritarum de præsentia & adoratione Christi in Sacramento, editæ anno 1432, conficiunt… Confer Resp. Taboritarum ad articulos Synodi Pragensis…: Idcirco, inquiunt, dicimus, quòd secundum Scripturæ Sacræ sententiam, sanctorum documenta doctorum, Catholicè est credendum, ore sincerissimè confitendum, totum Jesum ejusque verum corpus & sanguinem in sacramento altaris esse veraciter, sacramentaliter ac SPIRITUALITER, veri panis ac vini remanente substantiâ, non autem cum omnibus proprietatibus, tam Essentialibus, quàm accidentalibus, consequentibus idem ipsum corpus.
latin.594: Præterea parte 2. … Waldenses pag. 292. de Sacramento Eucharistiæ quatuor nobis divinam Scripturam credenda proponere perhibent, quorum Primum faciunt, quod Sacramentum hoc, panis & vinum sit. Secundum, quod panis ille sit verum corpus Christi, & vinum sit verus Sanguis Christi… Quibus quidem verbis Christi si quis præpostero ordine priùs velit intellectum obtrudere… ut aut nimis in altum se subvehat, hoc est, quod velit integrum Christum inibi viventem CORPORALITER seu personaliter præsentem corporibus nostris… aut è diverso minus sese in ima dejiciat … ut nullo modo Christum hic esse ferat, sed solum NUDUM & exsangue ac nihil operans in anima, SIGNUM… Tertium… Novum Testamentum… Quartum… panis ille sit participatio corporis Christi & Vinum Sanguinis ejus… Spiritualem manducandi Corporis Christi modum, excluso corporali, innumeris vicibus inculcantes…

pass_a.589: §. XIX. The Waldenses in England, celebrated under the Wycliffites’ name in the XIVth Age, are succeeded in the XVth AGE by the BOHEMIAN WALDENSES, surnamed HUSSITES from John Hus, Wycliffe’s Disciple, and through Wycliffe’s Writings brought from England into Bohemia by Jerome of Prague, excellently taught the true sentence against the Papacy.
pass_a.590: To him indeed the same happened that a hundred years later happened to Luther (of whom he had foretold with a certain prophetic spirit that from the ashes of the goose — i.e. his own, or Hus’s (by that name the Bohemians designate a goose) — a swan, or Luther, would rise again, whom the Papists would not reduce to ashes) — namely that he was less able to cast off at once the whole Papacy in which he had been nurtured; nay rather, as Luther at the Reformation’s beginning placed all his labor only in abolishing Indulgences, so this one placed all his labor in introducing and establishing Communion under Both kinds, Transubstantiation no less than Luther being dismissed, and even held in the same place with Consubstantiation, as is clear from Hus’s own Tract on the Sacrament of the Lord’s body and blood, which he wrote in the Constance prison in the Year 1415, ch. 2.
pass_a.591: yet Hus’s Followers, from the region in which they lived called Bohemian Brethren, and from a certain town or Castle named Tabor called Taborites, came nearer the truth concerning the Sacred Supper, having recognized both the tropical speech in the Institution words and the presence of Christ’s body in the Supper — but only Spiritual, not Natural and corporal; likewise eating to be performed with the mouth of faith, and hence peculiar to the faithful, not common to unbelievers. All this becomes clear from their various Confessions published in the XIVth and XVth Ages and comprehended by Balthasar Lydius, Pastor of Dordrecht, in the Year 1616 in one Volume of two parts.
pass_a.592: In the First Part Johannes Lucawitz, chief doctor of the Taborites, against Rokycana and the Prague Papists, thus confesses concerning the Sacrament of Christ’s Body and Blood: Concerning this Sacrament, he says, we hold this from the faith of scripture and sincerely believe in the heart, that the bread which Christ taking in His Supper gave His disciples to eat, and in its worthy perception through the Ministry of faithful priests left as a memory of His passion, is in its nature true bread, which by the pronoun This is pointed out in this sacramental proposition: This is my body, and with this the true body of Christ taken from the Virgin and handed over for us — not identically, not understanding material identity, but sacramentally, really and truly — which on account of its habitude toward Christ’s body is to be held in due reverence, and the faithful venerate it not as it is bread’s substance, but insofar as, as premised, it is Christ’s body, whose true body is to be believed to be in the same truly, sacramentally, SPIRITUALLY. Not however with all essential and accidental properties following it.
pass_a.593: Which words also make the first article of the Taborites’ Confession on the presence and adoration of Christ in the Sacrament, published in the year 1432… Compare the Taborites’ Response to the articles of the Prague Synod…: Therefore, they say, we say that according to Holy Scripture’s sentence and the holy doctors’ documents it is to be believed Catholically and confessed with most sincere mouth that the whole Jesus and His true body and blood are in the sacrament of the altar truly, sacramentally and SPIRITUALLY, the substance of true bread and wine remaining, not however with all Essential and accidental properties following that same body.
pass_a.594: Further in part 2… the Waldenses at p. 292 are said to propose four things divine Scripture would have us believe concerning the Eucharistic Sacrament: First, that this Sacrament is bread and wine. Second, that that bread is Christ’s true body and the wine Christ’s true Blood… But if anyone would first thrust an intellect on Christ’s words in a preposterous order… so that either he lifts himself too high — wishing the whole Christ living there CORPORALLY or personally present to our bodies… or on the contrary casts himself too low… so that he bears Christ to be here by no means, but only a BARE and bloodless Sign doing nothing in the soul… Third… the New Testament… Fourth… that bread is participation of Christ’s body and the Wine of His Blood… inculcating countless times the Spiritual mode of eating Christ’s Body, the corporal shut out…

589: §.XIX: the Waldenses celebrated in England under the Wycliffites’ name in Age XIV are succeeded in Age XV by the BOHEMIAN WALDENSES.
Surnamed HUSSITES from John Hus — Wycliffe’s disciple — taught the true anti-papal sentence through Wycliffe’s writings brought from England by Jerome of Prague.
590: Hus, like Luther a century later, could not cast off the whole Papacy at once — he focused labor on Communion under Both kinds, as Luther first on Indulgences.
Transubstantiation he dismissed no less than Luther, and even set with Consubstantiation (prison Tract at Constance 1415). He had foretold a swan rising from the goose’s ashes — Luther.
591: Hus’s followers — Bohemian Brethren / Taborites — came nearer Supper truth.

They recognize tropical Institution speech and Christ’s presence in the Supper — Spiritual only, not natural/corporal — eating by faith’s mouth, for the faithful not the unbelieving (Lydius’s collected confessions, 1616).
592: Lucawitz (chief Taborite doctor): the Supper bread is in its nature true bread — the ‘This’ of ‘This is my body’ points to that bread.

With it is Christ’s true body from the Virgin — not material identity, but sacramentally, really, and SPIRITUALLY; reverence for the habitude to Christ’s body, not for bread’s substance as such; not with all essential/accidental properties.
593: Those words also form article 1 of the 1432 Taborite Confession on presence and adoration.

Response to the Prague Synod: believe and confess the whole Jesus — true body and blood — in the altar sacrament truly, sacramentally, SPIRITUALLY, bread and wine substance remaining, without all following properties of the body in heaven.
594: Waldenses to Vladislaus (part 2): Scripture proposes four heads — (1) the Sacrament is bread and wine; (2) that bread/wine are Christ’s true body and Blood; (3) New Testament/covenant; (4) participation of body and blood.

Beware two ditches: lifting too high into CORPORAL/personal presence to our bodies, or sinking to a BARE bloodless Sign — they inculcate Spiritual eating, corporal shut out. Stop before §.XX (Lutheran comparison).
